Photograph: Shahrzad Rasekh/Reuters ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) ICE agent shoots and wounds man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas, officials say Anti-ICE protests break out in push for transparency as unnamed man is in serious but stable condition at hospital Associated Press Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.37 EDT Last modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) officer shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon in Texas ’s capital of Austin , local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene. The unnamed man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the city’s north side, Austin’s police chief, Lisa Davis, said at a news conference with the mayor and other city officials. The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not participate in the news conference and didn’t immediately respond to requests for details. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, Davis told reporters. Kirk Watson, Austin’s Democratic mayor, said he wants the city’s police department to be involved in the investigation so it can provide “clear, third-party eyes” in the process. Watson said he does not think it would be appropriate for ICE to conduct an investigation on its own. Austin residents have “a right to feel safe in their city”, Watson said. A proper investigation will only enhance credibility, he added. View image in fullscreen People speak during a demonstration where a man was shot in his vehicle by an ICE officer, on 20 September in Austin, Texas. Photograph: Joel Angel Juarez/AP Davis said she did not yet know the nationality of the person who was shot. The chief said there were not many facts she could provide so soon after the incident, but added that her department’s special investigation unit was at the scene. A dark blue Toyota Corolla was parked under an overpass with damage to its passenger-side door and what appeared to be bullet holes, local media reported. A large law enforcement presence was at the scene, along with a crowd of about a hundred protesters. Some demonstrators cursed at police officers holding riot shields, while others yelled out as passing cars honked in support of the protest. One man held a sign saying “Nobody is safe” and on the other side, “ICE Nazi”. Asked if Austin authorities knew where the involved federal agent is, given that agents have left states after previous shootings nationwide, the mayor said: “We do not know that. But my hope would be that, an agent that’s involved in an officer-involved shooting would not leave the city. Certainly not leave the state.” Greg Casar, a Democratic congressman representing parts of Austin, called for transparency as the shooting is investigated. View image in fullscreen Authorities deploy ‘non-lethal’ weapons near a demonstration where a man was shot in his vehicle by an ICE officer, on Sunday in Austin, Texas. Photograph: Joel Angel Juarez/AP “It is awful that this horror has come to our doorstep,” Casar told reporters. “For Austin to be safe, ICE should end its surge here.” The shooting comes as ICE surges enforcement across the country this summer, producing more than 50,000 arrests a month for the first time in its history in July and August. In July, an ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo of Houston, after federal agents driving unmarked vehicles pursued him while he was taking his construction crew to a job site. Also in July, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old Colombian man, was shot by an ICE officer in Maine. The officer is an army veteran who has struggled with serious mental health issues since early childhood and never should have been given a badge and gun to patrol American streets, several of his close relatives told the Associated Press. The administration’s enforcement efforts were widely condemned last winter after the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota. https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-iran-.text: LONDON — Britain believes Iran was involved in the incident at a British airbase used by the United States which saw five men arrested on suspicion of terrorism , U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said. Speaking to the BBC, Burnham said: "We will say more in due course but we can confirm ... that we believe Iran to have played a part.” Five British men in their 20s were arrested in the early hours of Sunday after Gloucestershire Police received a report of suspicious vehicles near RAF Fairford, which is used by the U.S. Air Force. They were arrested on suspicion of offenses under the Explosives Act and later, preparation of a terrorist act. Advertisement Advertisement After examination of the vehicles, authorities found no improvised explosive devices, but police said they recovered “a quantity of petrol.” The men were later released on bail but remain under investigation. Counter Terrorism Policing are leading the investigation into any potential motivation behind the incident. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said on Monday that “every possible angle” was being investigated, including “that this may be activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state.” Burnham’s comments came after U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed that the RAF Fairford incident “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor.” The U.K. prime minister said that the government has been "talking to our counterparts in the United States all week to explain what is happening here, how things are being done", and that he has "complete confidence in the way British security services are handling this." Earlier this year, the U.S. Air Force was authorized to use RAF Fairford to carry out “defensive” strikes on Iran. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned the U.K. in July that any British military base used by the U.S. to launch attacks would become a “legitimate target.” Advertisement Advertisement
